venue.name: 新百合トウェンティワンホール

events.factual_description: Kanagawa Kenmin Hall presents C × JAZZ Vol.2: Kento Tsubosaka × George Gershwin at Shinyuri Twenty One Hall in Kawasaki on Sunday, December 13, 2026, with a 3:00 PM start and 2:30 PM doors. The first half is solo piano and lists Gershwin repertoire including Jasbo Brown Blues from Porgy and Bess, Fascinating Rhythm, Three Preludes, Someone to Watch Over Me, Rialto Ripples and Rhapsody in Blue. The second half adds a string quartet for the first movement of Gershwin's Piano Concerto in F, They Can't Take That Away from Me, I Got Rhythm and a new Kento Tsubosaka work commissioned by Kanagawa Kenmin Hall. The announced quartet is Honoka Kishimoto, Shuga Hayashi, Kei Tojo and Anri Tsukiji. The Kawasaki performance is the fourth announced stop of a Kanagawa tour also visiting Zama on December 4, Kamakura on December 5 and Kaisei on December 12, and is presented with cooperation from Kawasaki Jazz 2026. Reserved-seat face values are ¥3,000 general and ¥500 for U24. General sale begins September 12; KAme member presale runs August 22 through September 11.

en.why_it_matters: The shape of the program is the hook. Tsubosaka starts alone with Gershwin, including Rhapsody in Blue, then changes the acoustic problem completely by bringing in a string quartet for the second half and ending the written program with his own newly commissioned work. That makes the evening a live argument about where Gershwin's jazz-classical vocabulary can lead a young Japanese improviser-composer now, rather than a respectful standards recital.
en.trip_verdict: If you are in Greater Tokyo/Kanto in mid-December, make room for the Kawasaki afternoon and use Shin-Yurigaoka as the anchor. The same ensemble and program have three earlier Kanagawa stops, so there is no need to chase another city unless December 13 does not fit.

es.why_it_matters: La forma del programa es el gancho. Tsubosaka empieza solo con Gershwin, incluida Rhapsody in Blue, y después cambia por completo el problema acústico al sumar un cuarteto de cuerdas en la segunda mitad y cerrar el programa escrito con una obra nueva comisionada a él. La noche se vuelve así un argumento en vivo sobre hasta dónde puede llevar hoy el vocabulario jazz-clásico de Gershwin a un joven improvisador y compositor japonés, no un recital respetuoso de estándares.
es.trip_verdict: Si estás en el área metropolitana de Tokio/Kanto a mediados de diciembre, haría espacio para la tarde de Kawasaki y usaría Shin-Yurigaoka como ancla. El mismo ensamble y programa tiene tres paradas previas en Kanagawa, así que no hace falta perseguir otra ciudad salvo que el 13 de diciembre no te funcione.
